topics.label: Introduction and learning objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This opening section welcomes students to the final lecture and outlines the core learning objectives concerning cancer therapies.

topics.label: Conventional cancer therapies and their limitations
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics discuss primary non-targeted treatment modalities including surgery, radiotherapy, and cytotoxic chemotherapy alongside their systemic toxicities and resistance mechanisms.

topics.label: Exploiting intrinsic cancer vulnerabilities and synthetic lethality
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics cover therapeutic strategies designed to exploit specific biological weaknesses in cancer cells, including hormone signaling dependence, cell-cycle checkpoint defects, and DNA repair deficiencies.

topics.label: Small-molecule kinase inhibitors and resistance mechanisms
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics focus on targeting oncogene-addicted kinase signaling with small-molecule inhibitors and the clinical challenges of drug resistance and bypass pathways.

topics.label: Monoclonal antibody and antibody-drug conjugate therapies
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine targeted cell-surface therapies utilizing naked monoclonal antibodies and antibody-drug conjugates.

topics.label: Cancer immunology and T-cell-directed immunotherapies
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the principles of cancer immune surveillance and modern immunotherapeutic approaches that harness T cells against tumors.

topics.label: Current challenges, future directions, and clinical realities in oncology
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics assess the broader clinical challenges, historical trends, genomic stratification approaches, and future directions in cancer treatment.
